en.intro: In this verse, Krishna lists the conditions of human life. Listen for the two words that sit together at the end, bhayam and abhayameva.
en.notice: Krishna puts bhayam, fear, and abhayameva, fearlessness, in the same breath. He does not say that fearlessness is the end of fear; he says both are his.
en.next: Next, Krishna says that nonviolence, honor, and dishonor all arise from him alone.
en.meaning: Understanding, wisdom, freedom from confusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, pleasure, pain, coming into being, ceasing to be, fear, fearlessness, nonviolence, evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and disgrace arise from me alone.

meaning_changed: "अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश सब उन्हीं से उत्पन्न होते हैं।" (The 'next' field in the script presents the content of the NEXT verse (verse 5) as if it belongs to this verse (verse 4). This verse's source explicitly includes 'evenness' (समता), 'contentment' (तुष्टि), 'austerity' (तप), and 'charity' (दान), but does NOT include 'nonviolence' (अहिंसा) in its list; nonviolence is in verse 5. Therefore, the 'next' field misdescribes the next verse by omitting 'evenness', 'contentment', and 'austerity' and adding 'nonviolence' which belongs to the following verse, constituting a borrowed/wrong_fact error.)

unsupported: "बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं।" (The Hindi translation explicitly states that these 20 qualities 'प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं' (these beings' various and different 20 qualities happen from me). However, the Sanskrit source only explicitly lists 17 items (बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, एव, च). The claim of exactly '20' (बीस) qualities is an unsupported factual claim not present in the source text.)

unsupported: "Listen for the two words that sit together at the end, bhayam and abhayameva." (The Sanskrit verse has 20 items, not two words at the end. The intro invents a listening focus that contradicts the source text.)

wrong_fact: "Next, Krishna says that evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and dishonor arise from him alone." (This is the content of the NEXT verse (verse 5), not the current verse (verse 4). The intro incorrectly attributes the next verse's content to this verse.)

wrong_fact: "Next, Krishna says that evenness, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and dishonor arise from him alone." (This is the content of verse 5, not verse 4. The next verse (verse 5) also includes nonviolence (अहिंसा) and freedom from confusion (असंमोहः) before evenness, and the intro for verse 4 already covers the full list of verse 4.)

unsupported: "कृष्ण जीवन की सभी स्थितियों को बताते हैं, ज्ञान से लेकर अभाव तक।" (The phrase 'सभी स्थितियों' (all situations) is an unsupported generalization. The verse lists specific qualities and conditions (like wisdom, forgiveness, fear, etc.) rather than stating that Krishna is describing 'all situations'.)

meaning_changed: "बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, एव, च।" (The Hindi translation omits key terms from the fixed English meaning: nonviolence (अहिंसा), evenness (समता), contentment (तुष्टि), austerity (तप), charity (दान), fame (यश), and disgrace (अपयश). It also changes the grammatical structure by adding 'च' (and) at the end instead of 'एव च' (indeed and), which slightly alters the emphatic 'alone' aspect of the verse.)
